subject: Query the script engine for current variables

messages.author: 42e5316f884713d9
messages.subject: Query the script engine for current variables
parts:
Hi,

Is there a way to ask the ScritpEngine for its current environment i.e. what variables and functions that have been defined similar to how the Environment tab in RStudio for GNU R?

I tried to follow the docs at http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/library/capture.html but no joy:

Renjin 0.9.2716
Copyright (C) 2018 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
Copyright (C) 2018 BeDataDriven
> d <- "bla"
> str(svmfit)
Error: object 'svmfit' not found
> 

Best regards,
Per

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Query the script engine for current variables
parts:
Hi Per,
The example you cite assumes the previous statements in the document have been evaluated:
engine.eval("library(e1071)");
    engine.eval("data(iris)");
    engine.eval("svmfit <- svm(Species~., data=iris)");

To get a list of variables defined in the global environment, you use the ls() function:

StringVector variables = (StringVector)engine.eval("ls()");

You can also access the global Environment object through Renjin's API:
RenjinScriptEngine renjinScriptEngine = (RenjinScriptEngine)engine;
Session session = renjinScriptEngine.getSession();
Environment global = session.getGlobalEnvironment();

Hope this helps,
Alex
